key_insight: Semi-supervised learning with ensemble consensus improves molecular graph prediction by leveraging unlabeled data without requiring tricky label-preserving augmentations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to boost accuracy and calibration in molecular property prediction models across diverse datasets and graph neural networks.
method: Train graph neural networks using an ensemble consensus objective on labeled and unlabeled molecular graphs.
Use agreement among ensemble members as the learning signal instead of hand-designed molecule augmentations.
Evaluate both individual ensemble members and full supervised ensembles across tasks and architectures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains across a diverse range of molecular datasets, task types, and GNN architectures, with improved robustness and reduced calibration error.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the ensemble consensus is configured and on the availability and quality of unlabeled molecular data.
paper_title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
